title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while a human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The car was in autonomous mode and did not slow down or stop before hitting the animal. This shows a perception or decision-making failure in how the system classified and responded to a small moving object in its path.

A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing data. It is not established whether the vehicle actually ran the stop sign or whether the duck strike involved a broader failure to detect and avoid obstacles. The incident prompted Avride to restrict testing on certain streets and conduct simulations to improve detection and avoidance, indicating the company identified a gap between its system's performance and the conditions it operates in.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents, which intensified their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in their community.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data and simulations. In response, Avride has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake. The company is now conducting controlled simulations to improve the technology and prevent similar situations without compromising overall vehicle safety. Local residents have saved the duck's eggs by placing them in an incubator.
